title: Product reindex job with wrapped indexing errors
name: Product reindex job

locateQuestion.prompt: Is there a defect in how errors are wrapped and given context as they move from the indexer to the job runner? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
locateQuestion.explanation: The bulk-write catch in productIndexer.ts wraps the error in an IndexingError but does not pass { cause: err }; it only copies the message into the text. isRetryable walks the cause chain with rootCause, so for these errors it sees the IndexingError itself, which is neither a SearchClusterError nor carries an errno code, and returns false. Transient 429/5xx responses and connection resets from the search cluster are therefore never retried, and batches are marked failed on the first hiccup. The catalog-load wrapper above it passes the cause correctly.

choiceQuestions.prompt: catalog.loadBatch rejects with an error whose code is ETIMEDOUT. How does runReindexJob treat it on the first attempt?
choices: It retries, because rootCause reaches the original error and isRetryable sees ETIMEDOUT
It records the batch as failed immediately, because IndexingError has no code
It rethrows and aborts the whole job
It retries forever, since attempt is reset per catch
choiceQuestions.explanation: The catalog wrapper passes { cause: err }, so rootCause follows .cause back to the errno error and isRetryable returns true for ETIMEDOUT; with attempt 1 < 4 the job sleeps and retries. The wrapper's own lack of a code does not matter because the root is checked, errors are caught per batch rather than aborting, and attempt increments in the for loop up to MAX_ATTEMPTS.

choiceQuestions.prompt: What is the purpose of the seen set in rootCause?
choices: It deduplicates log lines for repeated errors
It prevents an infinite loop if an error's cause chain contains a cycle
It caches root causes across calls for performance
It stops at the first non-Error cause
choiceQuestions.explanation: seen is local to each call and records every error visited; if a cause chain loops back on itself the while condition fails and the walk stops. It does not touch logging or persist between calls, and stopping at non-Error causes is done by the instanceof Error check, not by the set.

choiceQuestions.prompt: A bulk response comes back with HTTP 200 but body.errors set to true. Which statement about the indexer's handling is accurate?
choices: The batch counts as indexed because status is below 300
The SearchClient throws before indexBatch sees the response
A SearchClusterError is thrown with status 200 inside the try block and is then caught and wrapped by the surrounding catch
choiceQuestions.explanation: The condition res.status >= 300 || res.body?.errors is true, so SearchClusterError(…, 200) is thrown inside the same try, and the catch below wraps it in an IndexingError. It is not counted as indexed, the client returned normally, and there is no per-document fallback.
